stem: Which practice is most likely to help prevent delay in recognising important inguino-scrotal pathology in boys with abdominal pain?

options.text: Routine scrotal examination as part of assessment
Avoiding genital examination unless the family specifically requests it
Waiting for imaging before any examination
Restricting scrotal assessment to admitted patients

explanation: Routine scrotal examination as part of assessment is the best way to reduce missed inguino-scrotal pathology in boys with abdominal pain. A bedside genital examination can identify important findings early and prevent diagnostic delay.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Inguino-Scrotal Disorders in Children

optionExplanations.A: Correct because routine scrotal examination during assessment helps detect inguino-scrotal pathology early and reduces delay in diagnosis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because genital examination should not be avoided when it is clinically indicated in a boy with abdominal pain.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because abdominal findings alone can miss important scrotal pathology.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because examination should not be deferred until imaging; bedside assessment comes first.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because scrotal assessment should be performed when clinically relevant, not only in admitted patients.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
